H3 (label-agnostic consistency, companion): the VLM's own pred_morph will agree across the DECaLS/SDSS image pair for the same galaxy less often than a naive baseline of chance agreement computed from each survey's marginal prediction-class frequencies, evidencing depth-driven instability independent of the ground truth.
args.experiment: Using the 210-row table (105 galaxies x 2 surveys, linked by gid): (1) Compute acc_decals = mean(correct_morph) for survey=decals and acc_sdss for survey=sdss; report the raw paired difference. (2) Build the 2x2 paired contingency table over gid (decals-correct x sdss-correct: both-correct n11, decals-only n10, sdss-only n01, both-wrong n00); run exact/mid-P McNemar test on (n10,n01) with an exact binomial p-value (since discordant counts may be small) and report an odds-ratio/relative-risk with a Clopper-Pearson CI. (3) Build the two 3x3 confusion matrices (true morph x pred_morph), one per survey. From these, define smooth_collapse_rate(survey) = P(pred_morph='smooth' | true morph in {spiral, edge_on}, survey) and run a paired McNemar test on the per-galaxy binary indicator 'misclassified as smooth' restricted to the non-smooth-true subset (~70 galaxies if classes are balanced), reporting exact p and the DECaLS-minus-SDSS rate difference with CI. Also report the mirror check: false_structure_rate(survey) = P(pred_morph in {spiral, edge_on} | true morph='smooth', survey), to see whether deeper imaging instead promotes false spiral/edge-on calls on truly smooth galaxies (opposite bias). (4) For the label-agnostic consistency check: compute pair_agreement = P(pred_morph_decals == pred_morph_sdss) over the 105 galaxies (no use of morph/correct_morph), and compare to a null chance-agreement level = sum_c [P(pred=c|decals) x P(pred=c|sdss)] computed from the observed marginal prediction frequencies in each survey; test observed vs null with a permutation test (shuffle gid pairing 10,000x) or chi-square, reporting the observed-minus-null gap. (5) Report every number: acc_decals, acc_sdss, n11, n10, n01, n00, McNemar p (overall), smooth_collapse_rate_decals, smooth_collapse_rate_sdss, McNemar p (collapse), false_structure_rate_decals, false_structure_rate_sdss, pair_agreement, null_agreement, permutation p.
args.what_would_falsify: If McNemar's test on overall paired correctness gives p>0.05 AND the smooth_collapse_rate difference (DECaLS vs SDSS) has a confidence interval overlapping zero, H1/H2 are falsified -- i.e., the general VLM does not reproduce the known human/trained-CNN survey-depth morphology bias, which is itself a notable (negative) finding. args.minimal_publishable_claim: Even if the specific 'collapse-to-smooth' directional bias is not confirmed, a quantified, paired (same-galaxy) comparison of a general-purpose VLM's zero-shot morphology accuracy and prediction-agreement between deep (DECaLS) and shallow (SDSS) imaging of identical objects is a novel, useful benchmark result for the nascent use of general VLMs (as opposed to purpose-trained CNNs) in galaxy morphology pipelines, and the reported numbers (accuracies, McNemar statistics, confusion matrices, agreement rates) stand as a citable reference point regardless of which hypothesis direction holds.

A FULL STUDY = this battery (do every one the data can support; aim for >=5 analyses and ~8 figures/tables):

args.stat_tests: 6 total statistical tests were actually run: (1) H1 paired-accuracy McNemar exact binomial, (2) H2 smooth-collapse McNemar exact binomial, (3) mirror false-structure McNemar exact binomial, (4) agreement-vs-marginal-chance one-sided binomial, (5) agreement-vs-pairing permutation test (5000 shuffles), (6) agreement-by-true-class chi-square test. args.independence_check: The predictor variables in the LEAD analysis (pred_morph from DECaLS image, pred_morph from SDSS image) are outputs of the SAME VLM applied to two DIFFERENT input images (different survey cutouts) of the same physical galaxy -- so the two predictions are not derived from a shared representation of a single image, avoiding trivial circularity from re-using one image's embedding twice. 01_ideation.json.hypothesis: H1 (paired accuracy): Because SDSS imaging is shallower (r~22.2 vs DECaLS r~23.6) and loses resolved arm/dust-lane structure, the VLM's per-galaxy correctness (correct_morph) will be paired-worse for SDSS than DECaLS for the same gid, detectable via McNemar's test on the discordant pairs. H2 (error-direction / smooth-collapse): restricted to galaxies with true morph in {spiral, edge_on}, the VLM's SDSS misclassifications will disproportionately be predicted as 'smooth' (loss-of-feature default) relative to DECaLS misclassifications on the same galaxies -- a directional, not merely random, error asymmetry. H3 (label-agnostic consistency, companion): the VLM's own pred_morph will agree across the DECaLS/SDSS image pair for the same galaxy less often than a naive baseline of chance agreement computed from each survey's marginal prediction-class frequencies, evidencing depth-driven instability independent of the ground truth.
01_ideation.json.experiment: Using the 210-row table (105 galaxies x 2 surveys, linked by gid): (1) Compute acc_decals = mean(correct_morph) for survey=decals and acc_sdss for survey=sdss; report the raw paired difference. (3) Build the two 3x3 confusion matrices (true morph x pred_morph), one per survey. 03_sections.json.ABSTRACT: Automated morphological classification of galaxies traditionally relies on purpose-built machine learning models trained on labeled imaging datasets, raising questions about whether general-purpose vision-language models (VLMs) could offer a more flexible alternative. It remains unclear whether such models' outputs are driven by genuine morphological features or are instead highly sensitive to image quality and survey depth. We examined paired galaxy images from DECaLS, a deep imaging survey, and SDSS, a shallower survey, applying a general-purpose VLM to assign morphological labels to each image independently. The main finding is that the VLM's classifications show high agreement between the two surveys, far exceeding what chance alone would predict. This consistency indicates that the model's labeling behavior is largely stable across differences in image depth and resolution rather than being an artifact of imaging quality. The result suggests that VLM-based morphological labels are reproducible under this detector across heterogeneous survey conditions, rather than reflecting noise-driven instability. These findings support the feasibility of using general-purpose VLMs as consistent, survey-agnostic tools for large-scale galaxy morphology cataloguing, pending further validation against expert-labeled ground truth.
